arguments.title: Training appendix — April 18 shard-keeper outage
arguments.body:
## Misleading early branch

The first signals looked like generic ingest trouble, and a network-layer explanation distracted the investigation for a time. Symptom alerts fired, but the cause alerts did not. The confirmed cause was a producer–consumer contract mismatch: a label-name change shipped in shard-keeper, while rollup-service had not adopted the new name. The early green dashboards after the config push did not establish end-to-end parity.

## Confirmed impact

Ingestion was impaired for hours—about 5 hours 45 minutes until the incident was clean. The confirmed review found no data loss. Describe this as prolonged impaired ingestion, not data loss.

## Training point

When symptoms resemble a broad ingest or network failure, verify the actual label/key emitted by the producer against what each downstream consumer reads. Check cross-service parity and ownership before treating green service-local dashboards as proof of end-to-end health. Avoid a fragile rollback under pressure until its state and effects are understood.
